## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Huáyán jīng lún guàn* in 1 fascicle is [復菴](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%A9%E8%8F%B4) Fùān's compact synopsis of the *[Avataṃsaka](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010)* in the *lún guàn* 綸貫 ("through-thread") genre — a Sòng-period Buddhist literary form that aims to "thread through" (*guàn* 貫) a major sūtra by tracing the doctrinal-narrative thread (*lún* 綸) that connects its component parts. The genre originated in the Tang ([宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86) Zōngmì's now-lost *Huáyán lún guàn* mentioned in [the preface to T1738](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0016)) and was systematised in the Sòng.

**Abstract**

The work is conventionally datable to [復菴](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%A9%E8%8F%B4) Fùān's mature period, c. 1080 – 1130 CE. The bracket adopted here reflects this window. As *[the preface to Chéngguān's Qī chù jiǔ huì sòng shì zhāng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0016)* (T1738) indicates, Fùān's *Lún guàn* was widely regarded as Chán-leaning ("for Chán practitioners") and "sharp and direct" but less suitable for systematic doctrinal study. The work circulated in late-Sòng Chán-Huáyán synthesist circles, complementing the more scholastic commentarial tradition (Chéngguān-Zōngmì, Jìngyuán) with a Chán-flavoured contemplative reading.

The work is preserved in the Manji *Xù zàng jīng* (X220) collection.
